name: Direct hair implantation (DHI)

card.summary: A FUE variant that places grafts with a pen-style implanter; clinics promote precision, but independent evidence is scarce.
card.note: Reported to be costlier and slower than standard FUE; no controlled studies were found.

lead: Direct hair implantation (DHI) is a hair transplant technique in which follicles harvested from the back and sides of the scalp are placed into the balding area using a pen-like implanter, often associated with the Choi implanter pen, rather than into slits made beforehand. People choose it for a denser, natural-looking hairline and for restoring thinning areas, and clinics promote it as giving the surgeon fine control over the angle, direction and depth of each graft. [1][2]

DHI is a variant of follicular unit extraction (FUE), the approach in which individual follicular units of one to four hairs are removed with small punches of about 0.6 to 1.0 mm and left without a linear scar. [2] Wikipedia's hair transplantation article describes the broader field, including FUE and strip harvesting (FUT), but does not cover DHI as a separate method. [2]

Proponents describe DHI as combining the creation of the recipient site and graft placement in a single step. Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, reports that the technique is reported to be slower and costlier than standard FUE, at roughly 40 to 60 percent above it. [1] No controlled comparison of DHI against other FUE implantation methods has been published in the sources reviewed.

chain: Follicles are extracted from the donor scalp
Grafts are loaded into an implanter pen and placed at chosen angles
New hair grows in the hairline and thin areas over months
angle.text: The transplanted follicles continue to grow hair in the recipient area, which can rebuild a hairline or add density to thinning crowns. DHI's stated aim is more precise control of graft angle and direction, which proponents say helps a hairline look natural.

infobox: Small scattered dot scars at donor site; no linear scar [2]
FUE recovery under about 7 days per Wikipedia [2]

paras: In DHI, follicular units are extracted individually and loaded into the hollow needle of an implanter pen, which then places each graft directly into the scalp. Grokipedia says the pen creates the recipient site and deposits the graft in one motion, in contrast with techniques that cut recipient sites first. [1]

As with other FUE methods, the donor area is the "safe donor zone" at the back and sides of the scalp, where hair is resistant to male pattern balding. The concept of donor dominance was demonstrated by Norman Orentreich in the late 1950s, and the safe donor zone was defined by Walter Unger in 1994. [2]

Wikipedia describes FUE as leaving small, scattered scars and needing no suture removal, and notes that it takes longer, costs more and is harder to learn than strip harvesting, and that some surgeons report lower graft survival. [2] Its history includes a 2002 publication on FUE by Rassman and colleagues, and the first FDA-approved robotic systems, NeoGraft in 2009 and ARTAS in 2011. [2]
Wikipedia gives per-graft prices ranging from about US$1.07 in Turkey to US$7.00 in Canada, which illustrates why many people travel for procedures. [2]

General risks listed for hair transplantation include temporary shedding of existing hair ("shock loss"), infection, and effects of smoking, alcohol and blood-thinning medication on graft survival and bleeding. [2] Antibiotics are commonly prescribed after surgery. [2] No source examined reports risks specific to the implanter-pen method.

No studies found. A PubMed search for direct hair implantation with the Choi pen returned no results, and Wikipedia's hair transplantation article reports no quantitative success rates for the FUE family. [2]

timeline.event: Norman Orentreich's work on donor dominance underpins modern transplant surgery. [2]
Rassman and colleagues publish on follicular unit extraction. [2]
NeoGraft becomes the first FDA-approved robotic hair restoration device; ARTAS follows in 2011. [2]

quick.overview:
Direct hair implantation uses a hollow pen-like implanter, associated with the Choi pen, to place extracted follicular units directly into the scalp without pre-cut recipient slits. It is a variant of follicular unit extraction.

Clinics that offer it say it allows control of angle and direction, particularly at the hairline.
quick.mechanism: Follicles are extracted as in FUE, loaded into the implanter and inserted in a single step. Grokipedia describes creating the site and placing the graft together.
quick.risks: Grokipedia reports longer surgery, higher skill requirements, fewer grafts per session and higher costs than standard FUE; risks are those of FUE generally, including swelling, folliculitis and transection.
